AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #9 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How should broken glass be disposed of? (1 mark)
   A. Thrown in the yard
   B. Wrapped in thick paper and given to an adult
   C. Put in the compost
   D. Left on the floor

2. Which refuse can be put in the compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Tins
   B. Vegetable peelings
   C. Plastic bottles
   D. Batteries

3. Which of these can be made into a mop? (1 mark)
   A. A basin
   B. Strips of old cloth tied to a stick
   C. A chair
   D. A shoe

4. Which is a way of reducing waste? (1 mark)
   A. Throw things away quickly
   B. Buy more packages
   C. Reuse containers
   D. Burn tins

5. Where should clean PPE be stored? (1 mark)
   A. In a dirty box
   B. On the floor
   C. In a dry, clean place
   D. In a wet corner

6. Why should cleaning be done in an open place with drainage? (1 mark)
   A. To be seen
   B. So dirty water does not make a puddle
   C. To get wet
   D. To make noise

7. Why should torn gloves not be used? (1 mark)
   A. They are too clean
   B. They are too heavy
   C. They are too big
   D. They may not protect the hands

8. Which PPE is worn on the feet at school and in the garden? (1 mark)
   A. Gloves
   B. Overall
   C. Canvas shoes
   D. Dust mask

9. Which PPE protects the head from sun and dust? (1 mark)
   A. Gloves
   B. Gumboots
   C. Headgear
   D. Dust mask

10. What do you use to scrub gumboots? (1 mark)
   A. A soft brush with soapy water
   B. A hammer
   C. A knife
   D. A heavy stone

11. How should rubber gloves be cleaned? (1 mark)
   A. Throw them in a fire
   B. Wash them with soap and water while wearing them, then rinse and hang to dry
   C. Wash with a stone
   D. Leave them dirty

12. What should you do if your PPE is damaged? (1 mark)
   A. Hide it
   B. Throw it in a river
   C. Tell a teacher or an adult
   D. Keep using it

13. What is the use of labelling PPE? (1 mark)
   A. To hide it
   B. To make it heavier
   C. To tear it
   D. So each item goes back to its owner

14. Which kind of PPE is suitable for handling compost? (1 mark)
   A. Gloves and gumboots
   B. Shorts only
   C. A necktie
   D. A dress only

15. What should you do after cleaning PPE? (1 mark)
   A. Play in mud
   B. Wash your hands with soap
   C. Wipe them on clothes
   D. Eat without washing

16. How should you hold the cloth if you are right-handed? (1 mark)
   A. In the left hand while sewing with the right
   B. Under your foot
   C. In your teeth
   D. Above your head

17. Where should needles be kept? (1 mark)
   A. In a pin cushion or needle case
   B. On the floor
   C. On a chair
   D. In your mouth

18. About how long is the long stitch in long and short tacking? (1 mark)
   A. 2 metres
   B. 2 mm
   C. 2 cm
   D. 20 cm

19. What is the use of a scarecrow shirt made with tacking? (1 mark)
   A. It waters plants
   B. It is eaten
   C. It clothes the scarecrow using stitches
   D. It is a tool

20. When is even tacking most useful? (1 mark)
   A. When you do not want to sew
   B. Only for paper
   C. Only for straight seams that need no hold
   D. For curves and slippery cloth

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe how to make long and short tacking. (4 marks)

22. Explain the steps for dusting a room. (4 marks)

23. Why should a thread colour different from the cloth be used? (2 marks)

24. Explain three safety rules when cleaning. (3 marks)

25. What are tacking stitches? (2 marks)

26. Compare even tacking and long and short tacking. Say which is quicker and which holds more firmly. (4 marks)

27. Why should gumboots not be dried near a hot fire? (2 marks)

28. Plan a group project of making a scarecrow shirt using tacking. Give materials, steps, safety and how the group shares work. (5 marks)

29. Describe how to clean gumboots. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #9 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Wrapped in thick paper and given to an adult
   This prevents cuts.

2. B — Vegetable peelings
   Organic waste rots.

3. B — Strips of old cloth tied to a stick
   A cloth mop works well.

4. C — Reuse containers
   Reuse cuts down rubbish.

5. C — In a dry, clean place
   Damp PPE grows mould.

6. B — So dirty water does not make a puddle
   Dirty water can breed mosquitoes.

7. D — They may not protect the hands
   Holes let dirt and germs in.

8. C — Canvas shoes
   Canvas shoes protect feet.

9. C — Headgear
   Hats, caps and scarves cover the head.

10. A — A soft brush with soapy water
   A soft brush avoids damage.

11. B — Wash them with soap and water while wearing them, then rinse and hang to dry
   Washing with gloves on avoids touching dirt.

12. C — Tell a teacher or an adult
   Damaged PPE may not protect you.

13. D — So each item goes back to its owner
   Labels avoid mix-ups.

14. A — Gloves and gumboots
   They protect hands and feet.

15. B — Wash your hands with soap
   Hands can carry germs.

16. A — In the left hand while sewing with the right
   This is the usual way.

17. A — In a pin cushion or needle case
   Needles are sharp.

18. C — 2 cm
   The long stitch is about 2 cm.

19. C — It clothes the scarecrow using stitches
   Tacking holds the shirt pieces together.

20. D — For curves and slippery cloth
   Even tacking holds firmly.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mark a line; make a long stitch of about 2 cm on top; make a short stitch of about 0.5 cm underneath; repeat along the line; finish with a small back stitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Open windows; use a slightly damp clean cloth; dust from high to low; shake and wash the duster outside.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: The stitches are easy to see and to remove.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not mix chemicals; keep chemicals from children; wear gloves for dirty work; do not leave floors wet (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: Large, loose temporary stitches used to hold cloth in place before permanent sewing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for temporary, 1 mark for holding cloth.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: Even tacking is more even and holds more firmly; long and short tacking is quicker because each stitch covers more cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for each stitch description, 1 each for quicker and firmer.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: Heat can crack the rubber and spoil the boots.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for heat, 1 mark for cracking.

28. (5 marks)
   Answer: Materials: old cloth, needles, thread, scissors, chalk, ruler. Steps: measure and cut two pieces; pin; tack along sides; leave openings; sew firmly; stuff. Safety: count needles. Group: share tools, assign jobs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark materials, 2 marks steps, 1 mark safety, 1 mark teamwork.

29. (4 marks)
   Answer: Knock off lumps of mud; rinse; scrub with a soft brush and soapy water inside and outside; rinse again; dry upside down in the shade.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.
